# Brief: Ardennes Hour

## Idea

A two-player tabletop skirmish game set in the 1944 Ardennes, playable in under an hour with a deck of cards and no rulebook lookup.

## Problem and root-cause chain

Idea: a one-hour WW2 skirmish game. Why: existing skirmish games take a full evening. Why: their rules live in a book players must consult mid-game. Why: the designers put fidelity before flow. Root cause: the rules are not on the components. This chain reaches a root cause.

## User

Sam, 38, plays board games twice a month with one friend, has ninety minutes, and has bounced off two WW2 games because of rulebook lookups.

## Success metric and leading indicator

Fifty finished games reported by playtesters by 2026-12-31, each under sixty minutes. Leading indicator: three of the first five blind playtests finish without a rules question.

## Comparable products

Pending: the market pass did not run for this fixture.

## Scope

Smaller first version: one scenario, one deck, two forces, no campaign. It leaves out the campaign system and the third faction. It would still move the number. Recommendation: build the smaller version. Decision: open.

## Non-goals

- No solo mode.
- No app companion.

## Open questions for the author

- Is a card-driven activation system acceptable, or must it be dice? Assumption: cards.
